children: Sachin Kumar ET Intelligence Group: Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) are expected to post healthy year-on-year and sequential earnings growth for the September quarter, aided by buoyant refining margins, inventory gains and a reduction in fuel marketing losses. Brokers expect a 35-40% year-on-year increase in OMCs' revenue.

Ebitda is expected to register a double-digit sequential increase, supported by higher product prices during the quarter. Lower average crude prices and the full impact of the retail fuel price increase have helped improve petrol and diesel marketing margins, while elevated product cracks have supported refining profitability. The blockade around the Strait of Hormuz, disruption to three-four million barrels per day of refining capacity and a sharp rise in crude freight rates led to an expansion in refining cracks in Q2FY27.

Gasoil, gasoline and jet fuel cracks averaged $68.3, $30 and $72.9 per barrel, respectively, rising 15%, 9% and 26% quarter-on-quarter, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services. The broker expects companies under its coverage to report 23% and 15% year-on-year growth in revenue and net profit, respectively.

The June quarter was particularly difficult for OMCs because higher crude prices along with freight costs weighed heavily on marketing margins. OIL's total crude output is estimated to grow a strong 20% year-on-year, while ONGC's is expected to decline 6%. Gas output is likely to decline around 3% year-on-year for both.

With crude oil prices declining sequentially, oil realisation is expected to fall by nearly 6%. Emkay Global Financial Services expects gas realisation to decline for ONGC and remain broadly flat for OIL. RIL is expected to benefit from higher oil-to-chemicals (O2C) earnings, supported by stronger distillate spreads, improved petrochemical realisations and higher throughput.

City gas distributors are likely to see mixed trends, depending on sourcing costs, pricing and volumes, while Petronet LNG could benefit from higher terminal utilisation. GAIL's earnings are expected to moderate from the elevated levels seen in the June quarter as gas marketing margins have normalised.

title: Refining Gains, Lower Marketing Losses to Fuel OMC Q2 Earnings
